div.l: That p̉reued wel for oủeral there he cam
Atte wrastlyng / he wolde haue a wey the ram
He was short shuldred a thikke knarre
Ther ne was no dore / that he ne wolde heue of harre
Or breke it at a rennyng with his heed
His berd as eny sowe or fox was reed
And ther to brood as thought it were a spade
Vpon the cop right of his nose he hade
A werte / and ther on stode a tuft of heres
Rede as the bristelis of a sowes eres
His nose thrilles blake were and wyde
A swerd and a bokeler / bar he by his syde
His mowth as gret was as a gret furneys
He was a iangeler and a goliardeys
And that was most of synne and harlotries
Wel cowthe he stele corn . and tollen thries
And ȝit he hadde a thombe of gold parde
A whyt cote and a blew hood wered he
A bagge pipe wel cowthe he blowe and sowne
And ther with al he broughte vs out of towne
A gentil maunciple was there of a temple
Of which achatoᵘurs myghte take exemple
For to ben wise in beyinge of vitayle
For wheither that he payed or toke by tayle
Algate he wayted so in his achat
That he was ay biforn in good astat
Now is not that of god a ful faire grace
That such a lewed mannes wit shal pace
The wisdam of an heep of lerned men
Of maistres hadde he mo than thries ten
That were of lawe expert and curious
Of whiche ther were a doseyne in þᵗat hous
Worthy to ben stywardes of rente and lond
Of eny lord that is in Engelond
To make hym lyue by his ꝓpropre good
In honoᵘur detteles / but ȝif that he were wood
Or lyue as scarcely as hym list desire
And able for to helpen al a Shire
In eny caas that myghte falle or happe
